The following constructed data were recorded for a fixed gas sample at 290 K. The volumes and pressures have negligible uncertainty for this exercise. Use $R=8.31\ \mathrm{kPa\,dm^3\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

|Volume / $\mathrm{dm^3}$|Pressure / kPa|
|---|---|
|1.00|120.0|
|1.50|80.0|
|2.00|60.0|
|3.00|40.0|

verification.notes: Original Structure family S15-isothermal-data; variant 1/4.  No published question wording or artwork adapted. Independent review is recorded separately.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that these data are consistent with pressure being inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the amount of gas.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State why temperature must be controlled during this investigation.

steps.text: Calculate pressure × volume for at least two rows.
Every row gives PV = 120 $\mathrm{kPa\,dm^3}$, so pressure is inversely proportional to volume.
$n=PV/RT$.
$0.0498\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Changing temperature changes PV for a fixed amount of gas, so the effect of volume alone could not be identified.

title: Comparing gas samples
stem: Two separate containers each have volume 2.00 $\mathrm{dm^3}$, temperature 300 K and pressure 100.0 kPa. One contains $\mathrm{He}$ and the other $\mathrm{Ne}$. Both gases behave ideally. Their molar masses are 4.00 and 20.20 $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. Use $R=8.31\ \mathrm{kPa\,dm^3\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

parts.label: c

steps.text: The numbers of particles are equal.
$n=PV/RT$ gives the same amount of substance for equal pressure, volume and temperature.

They are equal because the gases have the same absolute temperature.
